correct_completion: I would apologise to her today.
full_sentence: If I were you, I would apologise to her today.
acceptable_variants: I would say sorry to her today.
I would call her and apologise.

options.text: I will apologise to her today.
options.why_wrong: 'If I were you' introduces a second conditional, so the result clause takes 'would', not 'will'.

options.text: I would apologise to her today.

options.why_wrong: The past simple describes a finished action and cannot give hypothetical advice after 'if I were you'.

options.text: I have apologised to her already.
options.why_wrong: The present perfect reports a completed action and does not fit an imagined, hypothetical situation.

grammar_focus: Second conditional with 'if I were you' (subjunctive 'were')
explanation: The stem uses 'if' with a subjunctive 'were' to imagine a situation that is not real, so the completion needs 'would' plus a base verb. Polish speakers often use a simple future form in this position, because Polish marks the conditional with a separate particle rather than a fixed modal verb in English.
translation: Gdybym był na twoim miejscu, przeprosiłbym ją dzisiaj.
